content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Some statements in the paper are unclear. For example, in the abstract section, what issues that seq2seq models suffer at the token level? What does token-level fitting mean? The code URL is also imcompleted. 
 
I understand the concept of fitting offset and potential-gain, but I can not understand why the proposed calculation method can reflect overfitting and underfitting at the token-level. 

The title is talk about seq2seq models while the experiments only use the Transformer-based models and two machine translation datasets. It would be better to verify the proposed method on more than one task and one type of base model. 

TOKEN-LEVEL FITTING ISSUES OF SEQ2SEQ MODELS
The paper focuses on the token-level fitting issues of the seq2seq model. In general, the paper needs more effort to make the proposed method clear. 

 
Some statements in the paper are unclear. For example, in the abstract section, what issues that seq2seq models suffer at the token level? What does token-level fitting mean? The code URL is also imcompleted. 
 
I understand the concept of fitting offset and potential-gain, but I can not understand why the proposed calculation method can reflect overfitting and underfitting at the token-level. 
 
The title is talk about seq2seq models while the experiments only use the Transformer-based models and two machine translation datasets. It would be better to verify the proposed method on more than one task and one type of base model. 


It would be better to use real experimental curve to support the statements in the paper. For example, the overfitting and underfitting in figure 1.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper analyzes token-level overfitting and underfitting in sequence-to-sequence models. In particular, tokens are grouped using 3 approaches: frequency, part-of-speech and prediction discrepancy (absolute probability difference between regular model and one which uses only the source and the previous target token). Overfitting/underfitting is detected with fitting-offset, which is the difference in epochs between the best fit (for a given token) and the global early stopping checkpoint. The paper also reports potential-gain (oracle accuracy improvement).
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
[Strengths]

The analysis across all 3 dimensions (frequency, part-of-speech, probability discrepancy) is fairly detailed.

Some results (e.g. the model is likely to underfit on high-frequency adjectives and nouns) might surprise some readers.

[Weaknesses]

The data scale is too narrow, which makes it hard to know if the findings are valid in different settings. Most experiments use 250k parallel sentences or less, although there are also experiments with 500k. Even 500k sentences is quite small. For example, the WMT'19 en-de training data has more than 38M examples (https://www.tensorflow.org/datasets/catalog/wmt19_translate).

Overfitting/underfitting is very likely dependent on the optimizer and regularization methods, but these are kept constant for each model.

There is no comparison to external baselines, which makes it difficult to know how good the models are.

The paper does not provide a clear path to improve models.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The anaysis appears to be rigorous, although important hyper-parameters (mentioned above) are kept constant. The paper is quite clear, although I would suggest not abbreviating words such as "adjectives" into "adjvs" in the main text. Some figures referenced in the paper are in the appendix. To my knowledge, the work in this paper is mostly novel. Most experiments should be reproducible, although we'd need to know which samples were selected for Europarl.
content.summary_of_the_review: The paper makes a detailed analysis of token-level overfitting/underfitting in seq-2-seq models. However, all experiments are conducted in a fairly small data regime, and important hyper-parameters are kept fixed.

content.summary_of_the_paper:
This paper addresses the overfitting / underfitting problem in seq2seq training.
They point out that overfitting and underfitting can occur simultaneously when it is being looked in token level.
They relate the phenomenon to a series of factors.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength:
This paper offers a better understanding to the overfitting problem of seq2seq model with a token-level perspective.


Weaknesses:
There are several misleading and ambiguous statements in the paper. 
The first statement of the paper:"Deep learning models tend to overfit because of their strong capacity and a massive number of parameters" is very misleading . Overfit happens in machine learning in every kinds of model.

"These criteria of easiness of learning targets are intuitive but coarse-grained, which are not associated with the training dynamics." <= This sentence is ambiguous. Having high frequency samples and low frequency samples are very common in machine learning problems, why it is not associated with the training dynamics. What dynamics are the authors referring to ? 

In general, the authors jump to the problem they want to address too quickly, without discussing how critical the problem is.

Intuitively, the model should overfit the low frequency samples and underfit the high frequency samples. This paper report an opposite phenomenon. It is better to discuss this more clearly.

The paper do not offer any solution to relieve the problem and improve the overall performance of seq2seq models.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
Clarity: The writing of the paper is fine but poor in theoretical clarity. A lot of intermediate explanation between observation and theory is missing.

Quality: Poor, this paper investigate a problem in a shallow way and do not provide any solution for improving the problem.

Novelty: Low, it is just a further look of an old issue.

Reproducibility: The codes are provided in the paper and others can replicate the results.
content.summary_of_the_review:
In general, the theoretical logic of the paper is ambiguous and hard to follow. 
This paper try to investigate a phenomenon in training NLP seq2seq models.
However, they do not relate how the overall study can benefit the performance in NLP tasks.
Finally, they do not offer solutions to solve the problem and improve the overall seq2seq model performance.

This paper is more like a technical report.
The amount of scientific content of this paper is not enough to be accepted in ICLR.

content.title: Token-level Fitting Issues of Seq2seq Models
content.TL;DR: We find that seq2seq models trained with early-stopping suffer from overfitting and underfitting at the token level. We identify three major factors that influence token-level fitting.
content.abstract: Sequence-to-sequence (seq2seq) models have been widely used for natural language process, computer vision, and other deep learning tasks. We find that seq2seq models trained with early-stopping suffer from issues at the token level. In particular, while some tokens in the vocabulary demonstrate overfitting, others underfit when training is stopped. Experiments show that the phenomena are pervasive in different models, even in fine-tuned large pretrained-models.  We identify three major factors that influence token-level fitting, which include token frequency, parts-of-speech, and prediction discrepancy. Further, we find that external factors such as language, model size, domain, data scale, and pretraining can also influence the fitting of tokens.
